artifact_groups.rationale: Visual Gödel: Escher's impossible staircase, Penrose triangle, and Magritte's pipe. Locally coherent, globally impossible — art that makes formal limits tangible.
Infinity in finite space: Escher's tessellations fill the plane without gaps. Scene-embedded — the environment itself demonstrates symmetry group tiling.
The treachery of images: this is not a pipe. Scene-embedded exploration of the gap between sign and signified — representation has limits.
The frame that lies: Magritte's windows where inside and outside collapse. Scene-embedded — the environment enacts the deception.
Pure Red, Pure Yellow, Pure Blue: Rodchenko's monochromes test whether meaning-free elements exist. Scene-embedded constructivist space.
What you see is what you see — but is it? Judd's specific objects: the minimalist paradox where meaning evacuates but significance remains. Scene-embedded.
The attempt to evacuate meaning keeps generating it. Scene-embedded darkness where absence becomes presence — the dark room as philosophical experiment.
Why artists see what mathematicians prove: synthesis across Escher, Magritte, Rodchenko, Judd. Scene-embedded reflection on visual epistemology.
Penrose tilings as cultural capstone: aperiodic order discovered independently in Islamic architecture and mathematical crystallography. Art and math converging on the same truth.
